transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thanks. Well, I guess what brings me in is that my head just feels really... foggy lately. I work as a personal care aide, and I’ve started making these little mistakes in my client notes. Like on Tuesday, I was filling out Mr. Abernathy's daily log. He’s this sweet older guy I help out, and he always wants to watch those old Westerns, you know, the black and white ones with John Wayne. We must have watched Stagecoach like five times this month alone. His TV is so loud too, it practically shakes the walls of his living room, which makes it hard to concentrate. 

But anyway, I was sitting there doing his notes and I just completely forgot what I was about to do. I just blanked. I keep doing that, just losing my train of thought right in the middle of things. It really isn’t like me at all—I'm usually really sharp with my paperwork, especially since I took some health admin classes back in college, but right now it's just all a fog.

Can you tell me more about these memory lapses? For example, do you forget things that happened recently, or do you also have trouble recalling information you used to know well, like names, routines, or how to do tasks you've done many times before?

Well, I don't really think it's like forgetting how to do things I know well... like my routines or anything. It's more just like what I just did, you know? Like, I'll be in the middle of a sentence or a task, and then it's just... gone. Like my brain just hits a wall. But speaking of routines, Mr. Abernathy has the strictest routine I've ever seen. Every morning, exactly at 8:00 AM, he wants his oatmeal. But it can't just be any oatmeal, it has to be the steel-cut kind, and it has to have exactly one teaspoon of brown sugar and a splash of milk. If I'm even a minute late or if I use the quick oats, he gets so fussy. It's kind of funny, actually, how set in his ways he is. I guess we all get like that when we get older, right? I mean, I'm 43 and I already have my own little quirks. Like, I can't drink coffee after 2 PM or I'll be up all night. But anyway, what were you asking? Oh right, the memory stuff. Yeah, I haven't really noticed forgetting old stuff or how to do my job, just the recent, in-the-moment kind of blanking.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Well, I guess... yeah, actually. Lately I just wake up with this heavy, empty feeling right in my chest. It's like I can still get through my shift, you know, and talk to Mr. Abernathy and the other clients, but inside I just feel sad and flat. It's hard to explain. Like I'm just going through the motions. Which is funny because usually I love chatting with my clients. I mean, just the other day I was talking to Mrs. Higgins—she’s another client of mine, lives down the hall from Mr. Abernathy. She used to be a baker, and she was telling me all about how she used to make these elaborate wedding cakes back in the 70s. Seven tiers, if you can believe it! She said the secret to a good sponge cake is room temperature eggs, which I never knew. I always just pulled them straight from the fridge. I tried baking a cake once for my niece's birthday, and it came out flat as a pancake. But anyway... yeah, I've just been feeling really down and empty lately, even when I'm listening to their stories. It's just hard to care about much.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or lacking energy most days, even when you haven’t been doing anything physically or mentally demanding?

Yeah, I really have. It's like... even on days when I'm barely doing anything, my body just feels completely worn out. Like, just helping one of my clients with a shower or carrying a couple of bags of groceries inside takes so much more out of me than it should. Speaking of groceries, the prices lately are just insane, aren't they? I went to the store the other day to pick up a few things for Mrs. Higgins—she wanted this specific brand of shortbread cookies, the ones in the blue tin, you know? And they were almost eight dollars! I remember when you could get those for like three bucks. It's ridiculous. I ended up getting her the store brand because she's on a fixed income, and she didn't even notice the difference, thank goodness. But yeah, by the time I got back from the store and put the bags on her counter, I just had to sit down for a minute. I felt like I'd run a marathon, and all I did was walk down aisle four.

Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or have others commented that you seem to be moving in slow motion? Or on the flip side, have you felt so restless or jittery that you couldn't sit still?

I haven't really noticed moving slower, and nobody's said anything about me moving in slow motion. And I'm not really jittery or anything either. I mean, my legs get a little stiff sometimes, but I think that's just from being on my feet all day. I bought these new shoes last month, those ones with the memory foam insoles? They were supposed to be the best for standing all day. The guy at the shoe store swore by them. He said his brother works in a warehouse and wears them for twelve-hour shifts. But honestly, I think they just make my feet sweat more. And the laces are too long, I'm always tripping over them. I should probably just go back to my old sneakers, even if the tread is worn out. But yeah, no, I don't think I'm moving slow or anything like that. Just regular, I guess.
Have you had trouble keeping track of things like appointments, conversations, or where you put your keys or other items?

Well, actually, yeah, that's kind of what brings me in. My head just feels really foggy lately. I've been making all these little mistakes in my client notes, which isn't like me at all. And I keep forgetting what I was just about to do. Like yesterday, I walked into Mr. Abernathy's kitchen to get his pills, and I just stood there staring at the refrigerator, completely blank. Speaking of refrigerators, his is making this awful buzzing sound. It started last week, just this low hum, but now it's getting louder. I told him he needs to call the landlord, but you know how landlords are. They'll take three weeks to send a guy out, and then the guy will just look at it, say he needs a part, and disappear for another month. I had a leaky faucet in my apartment last year, and it took them forever to fix it. Drip, drip, drip, all night long. It drove me crazy. I ended up putting a sponge in the sink just to muffle the sound so I could sleep. But anyway, yeah, the brain fog is getting pretty bad. I just can't seem to keep my thoughts straight.
Have you ever had a period of time when you felt down or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, and lost interest in most things you usually enjoy, lasting at least two weeks?

Yeah, that's... that's kind of where I'm at right now, actually. It's been a few weeks, I guess. Lately, I just wake up and there's this heavy, empty feeling sitting right in my chest. I can still get through my shift, you know, I can talk to my clients and smile and do the work, but inside I just feel so sad and flat. It's like going through the motions. Which reminds me, I have to go to the DMV to renew my registration, and talk about going through the motions. Have you been there lately? The lines are just unbelievable. I went last Tuesday on my lunch break thinking it wouldn't be too bad, but the line was out the door and wrapping around the building. And it was raining! Just this miserable drizzle. The guy in front of me had an umbrella that kept poking me in the shoulder, but he didn't even notice because he was screaming into his phone about a fantasy football trade. I don't even understand fantasy football. Why do people get so worked up over imaginary teams? My buddy Dave plays it, and he spends hours every Sunday just staring at his phone, getting mad at guys he's never met. It seems exhausting. But anyway, yeah, I just feel really down and hollow inside most of the time lately.
Have you noticed any difficulty learning new information or handling more complex tasks at work or home, like managing schedules, medications, or following instructions?

Well, yeah, actually. It's been getting kind of embarrassing, honestly. At work, I've had to start asking my coworkers to double-check my client documentation because I just keep messing up the details. And at home, my wife has had to take over paying some of the bills and keeping track of our schedule because I'm just not reliable with it right now. Which is crazy because she already has so much on her plate. She works at this bakery downtown, the one on 4th Street? They make these incredible sourdough loaves, but she has to be there at 4:00 AM to start the prep. I don't know how she does it. I tried waking up with her a few times just to make her coffee, but I was a zombie for the rest of the day. And the parking down there is a nightmare. She got a ticket last week because the meter ran out two minutes before she got back to her car. Two minutes! The city must be making a fortune off those things. They just installed those new digital meters, too, the ones where you have to type in your license plate number. I always transpose the numbers when I try to use them. But yeah, I'm just having a really hard time keeping track of things and learning new stuff lately.
Have you had any days where you felt so down or hopeless that you couldn’t get out of bed or take care of your usual responsibilities, or felt that life wasn’t worth living?

Well, I haven't missed any shifts, like I said, I still get myself up and go to work. But... yeah, there have been some mornings lately where I just lie there and think, you know, it really wouldn't be the worst thing in the world if I just didn't wake up. And that... that actually scares me a lot, to even have a thought like that. I'm not planning to hurt myself or anything, it's just this heavy feeling. Speaking of waking up, my neighbor got this new rooster. A rooster! In the city limits! I'm pretty sure that's against some kind of zoning ordinance. It starts crowing at, like, 4:30 in the morning. Every single day. I tried talking to him about it, but he just went on this whole rant about urban farming and sustainability. He's got these raised beds in his front yard now, growing kale and tomatoes. The tomatoes look pretty good, actually, but the kale is just getting eaten by bugs. I tried growing tomatoes once when I was in college, just in a pot on my balcony, but I kept forgetting to water them and they just shriveled up. But anyway, yeah... I don't want to hurt myself, but those thoughts in the morning, they really scare me.

Can you describe how long these feelings of sadness, low energy, and foggy thinking have been happening? Have they been continuous over the past two weeks or longer, and do they occur nearly every day?

Yeah, it's been pretty much every day. That low, guilty, foggy feeling has been hanging over me for about a month now. Just continuous, really. About a month ago was right around the time they started that construction on the highway near my house. Have you driven on I-95 lately? It's a complete disaster. They've got two lanes closed down for miles, and the traffic just crawls. I don't understand why they always decide to do these major road projects right when everyone is trying to get back into their normal routines. It's like they want us to be miserable. I saw a guy the other day get so mad he actually got out of his car and started yelling at a construction worker. The worker was just holding a stop sign! He didn't design the highway. People are just so on edge these days. I think it's the weather, too. It's been so unseasonably warm, but then it drops 20 degrees in one day. My joints can't take it. But yeah, to answer your question, it's been about a month of just feeling this way every single day.
Have you experienced any days in the past month where you felt little pleasure or interest in doing things you usually enjoy, almost every day, all day?

Well, no, not really. I mean, I still try to do things I like when I have the energy, you know? Like, I still watch my shows and everything. Speaking of shows, did you see the finale of that baking competition on Channel 5? I couldn't believe they sent Marco home. His sugar sculptures were amazing, way better than Sarah's. Although I guess her flavor profiles were a bit more refined. My wife watches it with me sometimes, when she's not exhausted from the bakery. We tried making one of the recipes from the show once, a chocolate lava cake. It completely collapsed. Chocolate everywhere. The dog loved it, though. We have this golden retriever, Buster, and he will eat literally anything that hits the floor. He ate a whole stick of butter once that rolled off the counter. I had to call the emergency vet, and they were like, just watch him, he'll probably just have a stomachache. He was fine, just slept for like twelve hours. But yeah, no, I haven't really lost interest in stuff I enjoy, I just haven't had the energy to do as much of it.
Have you noticed that you’re not getting as much pleasure or interest out of the things you usually enjoy, even when you do them?

Well, I guess... maybe a little bit? Like, I still watch my shows, but sometimes I'm just staring at the screen and not really caring who wins. It's not like I don't want to do them, it's just... I don't know, the spark isn't really there as much. Which is a shame, because we just got this new TV. My wife surprised me with it for my birthday. It's one of those OLED ones, the picture is so clear it almost looks fake, you know? Like you're looking through a window. We had to get a new TV stand for it, too, because our old one was too small, and let me tell you, putting that thing together was a nightmare. The instructions were just pictures, no words, and they gave us like three extra screws, which always makes me think I missed a step. I spent three hours on the floor with an Allen wrench. My knees were killing me the next day at work. Being a personal care aide is hard enough on the joints without spending half the weekend assembling furniture. I had to help Mr. Henderson into his wheelchair the next morning, and I swear my back popped so loud he asked if I was okay. He's a sweet guy, Mr. Henderson. Used to be a jazz musician in the sixties. But anyway, yeah, I guess I'm just not getting the same kick out of things right now, even when I force myself to do them.
Can you tell me more about not getting the same enjoyment out of things—has this been happening every day, or is it more occasional?

Well, I guess... I haven't really thought about if it's every single day. Maybe not every day? It's hard to keep track. Time just sort of blends together lately. Speaking of time blending together, the daylight saving time switch really messed me up this year. Did it mess you up? I feel like I'm waking up in the pitch dark and driving home from work in the pitch dark. It's depressing just thinking about it. I was telling my wife the other day, we should just move to Arizona or somewhere they don't do the time change. My cousin lives in Phoenix, and he says you just get used to the heat. He's got a pool, though. If I had a pool, I wouldn't care how hot it gets. I'd just float around all day with a cold drink. We looked into getting one of those above-ground pools for the backyard, but the city permits are a total nightmare. You have to get approval from the zoning board, and they meet like once a month on a Tuesday morning when everyone is at work. It's a racket, I swear. So we just got Buster a little plastic kiddie pool instead. He loves it. He just sits in it and bites at the water. But yeah, I don't know if the enjoyment thing is every day, I just haven't really noticed a pattern.

Over the past month, have you experienced at least five of the following nearly every day: feeling sad or empty, loss of interest or pleasure, significant changes in appetite or weight, trouble sleeping or sleeping too much, feeling slowed down or restless, feeling worthless or guilty, or having trouble concentrating?

Well, yeah, if I think about it... that low, guilty, foggy feeling has been hanging over me for about a month now. Foggy is actually a really good word for it. It's exactly like how my windshield gets in the mornings because the defroster in my Honda finally gave out. I tried fixing it myself last weekend, watched a couple of YouTube videos, but you have to take the whole dashboard apart just to get to the heater core. There are all these little plastic clips holding the panels together, and they just snap if you look at them wrong. I broke two of them and ended up just having to use duct tape. 

I really need to take it to Tony, my mechanic down on 4th Street, but he just raised his labor rates again. He said it's because of the supply chain. Everything is the supply chain these days, right? Even at the grocery store, they were out of the specific brand of dog food Buster likes. We had to get him the chicken and rice one instead of the beef, and he gave me this look like I had completely betrayed him. Made me feel terrible, honestly, like I'm letting the dog down. But yeah... what were you asking? Oh, right, the symptoms. Yeah, it's been about a month of that foggy stuff.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight over the past month?

Well, I haven't really noticed anything with my weight or my appetite, honestly. I mean, I eat when I'm supposed to, mostly. My wife usually makes dinner, and she's been trying out all these new recipes she found on Pinterest. Last night she made this... I don't even know what to call it. It was like a zucchini noodle thing with a peanut sauce? It wasn't bad, actually, but it definitely wasn't pasta. She's on this big kick about eating healthier because her sister just got diagnosed with high cholesterol. 

Her sister, she's a trip. She lives out in Oregon and runs this little artisan soap shop. She sends us these boxes of soap every Christmas, and they always smell like pine needles and lavender. It's nice, but I'm more of a regular bar soap kind of guy, you know? Just give me Irish Spring and I'm good to go. The fancy stuff always leaves a weird film on my skin. Anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right, my weight. Yeah, no, I don't think it's changed. I'm wearing the same pants I always wear for work, so I guess it's all about the same.
Over the past month, have you felt worthless or guilty nearly every day?

Well, yeah, actually. That's... that's been pretty heavy lately. I keep replaying what I should have done for my tío before he died, like calling more or visiting sooner, and I end up feeling like I just completely failed him as family. It's this awful guilt that just sits there. My tío, he was always so good to me when I was a kid. He used to take me fishing down at the lake, and we'd sit out there for hours. He had this old aluminum boat that leaked a little, so one of us always had to bail water with a cut-in-half milk jug. I always thought I'd get a boat like that someday, you know? Just a simple little dinghy to take out on the weekends. 

I was actually looking at boats on Craigslist the other night, just seeing what's out there. There was this guy selling a pontoon boat for dirt cheap, but he said the motor was seized up. I don't know the first thing about fixing a boat motor. It's probably like fixing that heater core in my Honda, just a huge headache waiting to happen. Plus, where would I even park a pontoon boat? My driveway is already cramped with my wife's SUV and my car. We'd have to pay for slip fees at the marina, and those are outrageous these days. But yeah, the guilt... it's just been really hard to shake that feeling about my tío.
Over the past month, have you felt little interest or pleasure in doing things you usually enjoy, nearly every day?

Well, I don't think so, no. I mean, I still like doing the things I normally do. Like, I still watch the game on Sundays. Though, honestly, the games haven't been that great lately. The referees are just throwing flags for every little thing now. You can't even tackle a guy without getting a penalty for roughing. It's really changing the whole dynamic of the sport, you know? My buddy Dave—he's the one I usually watch the games with—he was saying they should just put flags on the players and call it a day. 

Dave actually just got back from a trip to Florida. He went down there to visit his parents in this big retirement community. He said they have golf carts everywhere, like, people just drive them to the grocery store and the bank. He sent me a picture of his dad's golf cart, and it's got custom rims and a stereo system. Can you imagine? A golf cart with a subwoofer. I told him he needs to bring one back up here, but he said the battery wouldn't last in the cold weather. Which makes sense, I guess. Batteries always die faster when it's freezing. Like my phone, if I leave it in the car overnight in the winter, it's completely dead by morning. But yeah, no, I'm still interested in my regular stuff.
Over the past month, have you felt little interest or pleasure in doing things you usually enjoy, nearly every day?

Wait, didn't you just ask me that? Like I was just saying, no, I don't think so. I still enjoy things just fine. Even at work, I still get a kick out of it. I'm a personal care aide, mostly helping out seniors, and I still really like hearing all their stories. 

Like Mr. Henderson, this guy I help out on Tuesdays, he was just telling me about how he used to work at the old Ford plant. He actually just bought this massive model train set that takes up his entire living room. His daughter is absolutely furious about it because she says it's a tripping hazard, and she's the one who has to vacuum around it. She's a character, honestly. She works over at that bakery on 4th Street, the one with the really good sourdough? Man, I tried making sourdough a couple years ago when everyone was doing it. I had this starter in a mason jar on my kitchen counter, and I swear it started smelling like old gym socks after a week. My wife made me throw it out before it gained sentience. I think you're supposed to feed it flour every single day, which just seems like having a really boring pet, if you ask me. I don't have the patience for that. 

But anyway, what was I... oh, right. Yeah, no, I haven't lost interest in my hobbies or anything like that. Same as I said a minute ago.

Over the past month, have you had at least five of the following nearly every day: feeling sad or empty, loss of interest or pleasure, trouble sleeping or sleeping too much, feeling slowed down or restless, feeling worthless or guilty, or having trouble concentrating?

Well, let's see. You just asked about a whole list of things... sad, guilty, trouble sleeping, concentrating... yeah, I'd say I've had a bunch of those. That whole low, guilty, foggy feeling has been hanging over me for about a month now, pretty much every day. It's just this heavy cloud, you know? 

Speaking of clouds, the weather has been absolutely miserable this past month, hasn't it? It feels like it's rained almost every single day. I had to go buy a new umbrella because my old one blew inside out during that storm we had a couple weeks ago. It was one of those cheap ones you get at the drugstore when you're caught in a downpour. I finally went online and ordered one of those fancy windproof ones that are supposed to withstand, like, hurricane-force winds. The guy in the video was standing in front of a giant fan with it. It hasn't arrived yet, though. Shipping is taking forever these days. I ordered some new non-slip shoes for work, too, because the floors at the assisted living place get so slick when they mop. The janitor there, Hector, he uses this lemon-scented cleaner that smells exactly like those lemon drop candies my grandma used to keep in a little glass dish on her coffee table. They were always stuck together in one giant clump, so you had to chip a piece off if you wanted one. But yeah, to answer your question, it's been about a month of feeling that way.
